paragraphs: Bar Dalia. [Yerushalmi Eruvin 6:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Eruvin.6.8.8): "The people of Bar Dalia are not particular about their perutah"; from this it appears that it is a place name.

In Berakhot 14b and [Zevachim 33b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.33b.5), Rabbi Yohanan says: “Bardela taught.” In [Yerushalmi Kilayim 1:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Kilayim.1.6.3), Rabbi Yohanan says: “I brought it from Bar Dalia.”

Rav Acha Bardelai appears in [Sukkah 26a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.26a.8), and Abba Kohen Bardela in [Bava Metzia 10b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.10b.7). Ahavat Tzion VeYerushalayim discusses the Kilayim passage at length, arguing that it should read “from the school of Levi.”[^3]

notes.text: Bardela is the teacher in “Bardela taught,” not a person called Teni. Hyman’s place-name inference and the proposed “school of Levi” reading remain separate suggestions.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 1:6 contains “from Bar Dalia.” This occurrence does not decide Hyman’s place-name inference or the separate Ahavat Tzion VeYerushalayim proposal, whose exact text was not inspected.

The linked Eruvin speaks of the people of Bar Dalia, and Kilayim has “from Bar Dalia.” In Zevachim, Rabbi Yochanan introduces a teaching of Bardela. [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=783&lang=en) cites that use and reports that Rashi takes Bardela as a sage’s name. Hyman’s place-name conclusion and the alternative “school of Levi” remain separate readings.
